newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends lower, just above lifetime lows.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends lower, just above lifetime lows.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures settled lower and just above their lifetime lows after being hit by late fund-related selling, traders said.
"Rosenthal Collins was a key buyer last week, but they turned seller late today," a trader said. "In the last hour they must have sold two million Dec -- 500,000 of that came in the last 15 minutes."

Monday's USDA inspection report also raised renewed concern over stiff global export competition. The report showed that during the week ended Oct. 17, wheat inspections were up from the previous week but lagged year-ago levels.

KCBT wheat ended one to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 6-1/2 cents at $4.23-1/2. The lifetime low in Dec wheat is $4.21. March set a new life-of-contract low at $4.27 before settling down 3-1/2 cents at $4.08.
Traders said Cargill's purchase of around two million July bushels helped boost that contract relative to nearby months.

Monday's price action enabled the Dec/March inverse to narrow further. The spread, which traded in excess of 20 cents per bushel last week, traded as narrow as 17-1/2 cents and closed at an "on paper" value of 15-1/2 cents.
